resources.string: Darts
Flick darts at the board: count down from 501 or play Cricket.
Practice
Throw on your own and beat your best average.
Throw against 1 to 3 computer players.
Your hand
How steady you throw. A steadier hand means less wobble.
Rock steady
Very little wobble.
Pub regular
A little wobble, like a keen amateur.
Nervous
A lot of wobble: a real challenge.
Darts game
Count down to zero, or close the Cricket numbers.
Count down to exactly zero. The classic match.
A shorter count down to zero.
Cricket
Close 20 to 15 and the bull, then out-score your rivals.
Double out
On: finish on a double or the bull. Off: any dart can finish.
Double in
On: your score only starts once you hit a double.
Bowling
Aim, swipe and curve the ball into the pocket for a strike.
Bowl on your own and chase a perfect 300.
Bowl against 1 to 3 computer players.
Bumpers
Rails along the lane keep the ball out of the gutters.
Aim guide
Shows the path your ball will take down the lane.
Drag on the board to move the reticle, then flick up to throw. Soft flicks sag low.
In 501 you must finish exactly on zero with a double. Go too far and the visit is a bust.
In Cricket, close 20 to 15 and the bull with three marks, then score on numbers rivals leave open.
Slide the ball to set where it starts, then swipe up. Curve your swipe to hook the ball.
Aim for the pocket beside the head pin for the best chance of a strike.
A spare scores the next ball as a bonus, a strike the next two. The tenth frame can give a third ball.
